instruction: Find LEGO sets for kids and arrange them starting with the most expensive.

metadata.explanation: Task requires searching for LEGO sets for kids on kohls.com and sorting by price high-low. Similar pattern to original with different product. Evaluator checks breadcrumbs and sort order using existing check_direct_json_object function.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks for LEGO filter/breadcrumb in both CSS classes and URL parameters
Evaluator correctly checks for Kids filter/breadcrumb in both CSS classes and URL parameters
Evaluator correctly checks for Price High-Low sort selection via breadcrumb ('Price High-Low') and URL parameter ('S=5')
Evaluator correctly checks that no unexpected filters are present (is_other_exist: false)
Getter uses active_tab_html_parse with category='class&url' which can extract both CSS class elements and URL parameters
Metric uses check_direct_json_object which performs exact key-value comparison
Minor issue: Evaluator only verifies sort option is SELECTED but does not verify products are actually DISPLAYED in price high-low order - assumes UI state matches sort selection
Case sensitivity handling is correct: getter normalizes to lowercase, expected values already use lowercase
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding verification that actual product prices on the page are in descending order to fully verify 'arrange them starting with the most expensive'
Could add extraction of first few product prices and verify price[0] >= price[1] >= price[2] to confirm sort worked
